## HEADLINE

The approved analytical core is **executed and validated**. The literal enrichment step (gseapy + `GO_Biological_Process_2021`) **could not be executed in this capsule**, and I did not substitute a proxy library. Therefore **the question's answer (the lowest-adjusted-p-value GO cellular process) is NOT produced by this run**, and I am not guessing it. Below: what blocked it (Rungs 1→3, in order), the completed DE result, the validated prerank engine, the stability flag you asked for, and the single artifact that unblocks the literal answer.

---

## 1. BLOCKER LADDER — executed in order

**Rung 1 (re-verify provisioning) — FAILED, definitively:**
- `pip install --retries 2 --timeout 8 --index-url https://pypi.org/simple gseapy` → DNS `Temporary failure in name resolution`; aliyun mirror → same. No `PIP_INDEX_URL`/`http_proxy`/`PROXY` set; no pip cache/wheelhouse anywhere.
- **Not just DNS — no route at all**: raw-IP TCP to 1.1.1.1:443, 8.8.8.8:53, 9.9.9.9:53, 151.101.0.223:443 (PyPI/Fastly), 140.82.112.4:443 (GitHub), 104.16.132.229/172.67.16.30:443 (Cloudflare) → all `[Errno 101] Network is unreachable`. Manual hand-built DNS UDP query to 8.8.8.8/9.9.9.9/1.1.1.1 → unreachable. So no "resolve-by-IP" workaround exists.
- Tools: `R`, `Rscript`, `conda`, `mamba`, `micromamba`, `uv` all MISSING. `pip list` = numpy 2.4.4, pandas 3.0.2, scipy 1.16.0, statsmodels 0.14.6, patsy, openpyxl (+stdlib).
- **Filesystem scan re-run WITHOUT `-xdev`** over every mount (`/` tmpfs, `/usr` ext4-ro, NFS `.actor-venv`, NFS `/workspace`) for `*.gmt`, `*.gmt.gz`, `*msigdb*`, `*GO.db*`, `*org.Hs*`, `*.obo*`, `*gaf*`, `*goa_*`, `*gene2go*`, `*enrichr*`, `*gseapy*`, `*Reactome*`, `*pathway*`, `*term2gene*`, `*hsapiens*`, `*.whl`: **only kernel modules/perl unicore false positives — zero gene-set resources**. Content grep for `GO:0006915`/`GO_Biological_Process`/`Biological Process` in `/usr/share`, `/etc`, `/usr/lib/python3/dist-packages`: no hits.
- Full capsule tree incl. hidden files: exactly `data/counts_raw_unfiltered.csv`, `data/ensg_to_gene_name.tsv`, `data/sample_layout.csv`, `task.json` (md5s recorded in the log). No second metadata/matrix file ships with the inputs.

**Rung 2 — N/A:** gseapy is not installable, and the package (with any bundled library) does not exist on disk.

**Rung 3 — PARTIALLY satisfied:** the gseapy-equivalent prerank engine is built and validated (below), but **"GO Biological Process annotations in any obtainable offline form" do not exist in this environment** — nothing obtainable, not just not pre-downloaded.

**STOP CONDITION invoked:** no hand-written proxy collection was used as an answer; deliverable = completed DE + validated engine + explicit blocker statement.

## 2. COMPLETED DIFFERENTIAL EXPRESSION (group 9 `Cisplatin_IC50_CBD_IC50` vs group 3 `DMSO`)

Preprocessing exactly as approved: 63,677×30 → 53,636 mapped → drop 10,041 unmapped → sum-collapse multi-ENSG symbols (Y_RNA 773, U3 44, U6 34…) → filter ≥10 counts in ≥3 samples → **universe A = 18,100 symbols**. Note: 1,416 of those "symbols" are ENSG IDs used as `gene_name` by the supplied annotation and can never match a GMT.

DE (in-script NB2 re-implementation; no R/pydeseq2): median-of-ratios size factors, `~0 + Group` on all 30 samples (rank 10, residual df 20), df-corrected method-of-moments dispersion shrunk to the mean-dispersion trend (prior df 2), Wald contrast, t(df) reference.
- **Diagnostics you asked for**: size factors 0.289–1.860, Spearman(size factor, library size) = **0.9964** (3_1 = 0.289, 9_2 = 0.377); BCV 10/25/50/75/90% = 0.036/0.047/**0.074**/0.156/0.280 with the trend saved per bin; Wald z mean +0.006, sd 2.417, λ_median 4.32, QQ slope 2.417. Model-free cross-check of the (low) dispersion: average within-group SD of log2 CPM for genes ≥10 CPM everywhere = 0.075 ⇒ implied BCV ≈ 0.05, i.e. the tight BCV is a property of these replicates, not an estimator artifact.
- **Engine self-calibration** (5 matched null sims + 3 spike sims): dispersion ratio to truth 0.96; **type-I error 0.047 at nominal 0.05 with the t(df) reference (0.061 with the normal reference)** — that is why the reported p-values use t(20); power 86% for a 1.8× spike; log2FC is attenuated (recovered 0.60 vs true 0.85 log2), a small-sample NB-MLE property to keep in mind for a log2FC ranking.
- **Primary result**: 6,014 genes p<0.05, **3,712 padj<0.05** (3,435 within universe B), 4,962 padj<0.10, 1,945 |LFC|>0.5, 415 |LFC|>1. Top by p: GDA, ADGRF1, FDXR, NR2F2, AEN, KIAA0040, SMAD3, INKA2, BTG2, TP53INP1 — a canonical p53/DNA-damage set (expected for cisplatin).
- **Sensitivities**: additive `treatment + serum_starvation` design → 7,533 p<0.05, Spearman vs primary **0.722**, median |Δlog2FC| 0.088; leave-out 3_1 → Spearman **0.959**, median |Δlog2FC| 0.030 (depth-fragile replicate is NOT driving the ranking); starved 10-vs-4 → Spearman **0.298** (different biology, reported only).
- **Ranked lists written (prerank-ready, `Name \t Score`, no header)**: primary log2FC on universe A (18,100) and universe B (12,910, CPM≥1 in all 10 groups), plus `-log10(padj)·sign` and signal-to-noise variants.
- **Two material findings about the pre-specified primary ranking**: (i) on universe A the metric extremes are artifacts — 7 genes with |LFC|>5 (max ±24.3), **all 7 zero-inflated**, and universe A vs B share only **56/500** of their top-500; (ii) top-500 Jaccard between log2FC and the p-based metric is only 0.05 on A vs 0.32–0.36 between the two statistical metrics. Headline answer still comes from the pre-specified primary log2FC metric, but **universe B is the file I would feed gseapy** (evidence in §3).

## 3. gseapy-EQUIVALENT PRERANK ENGINE — validated (`analysis/nblib.py::Prerank`)

Semantics match `gp.prerank`: weighted p=1 classic running sum, NES by same-sign permutation mean, GSEA sign-normalised nominal p, **FDR = Benjamini-Hochmann across all tested gene sets** (= gseapy's "FDR q-val"), min_size 15 / max_size 500, 1000 permutations, seed 42.
- **I found and fixed a real bug during validation**: my first null permuted metric weights at fixed hit positions, which makes a genuinely coherent set invisible (SPIKE_UP_strong: NES 1.00, p 0.52). gseapy permutes the metric and re-sorts, i.e. the set occupies uniformly random *positions*; corrected implementation samples positions from random permutations (verified uniform: mean 9052/sd 5227 vs theoretical 9050/5225). Both variants are in the log as a negative control on null construction.
- **Validation results** (N=18,100, 1000 perms, 1.2 s): 5/5 coherent spiked sets recovered with |NES| 3.75–7.80 and p ≤ 0.0068 and occupying the five lowest FDR ranks; a zero-effect spike returns p = 1.0; 120 true-null random sets → 1.7% p<0.05, **0% FDR<0.05**, median FDR 1.00; size filters honoured (size-14 and size-600 sets excluded); deterministic under fixed seed; known-answer sets (the set equal to the top-20 / bottom-20 / 20 random genes) give NES +4.61 / −4.73 / p 0.32 with correct signs.
- **Null control on the REAL metric** (100 random sets, no biological meaning — wiring/negative control only): universe A → min FDR 0.538, 6% of random sets p<0.05, max |NES| **3.88** (the ±24 artifact genes inflate NES); universe B → min FDR **1.000**, 1% p<0.05, max |NES| **1.74**. Clean behaviour only on universe B.
- Projected cost of the literal run (~7,600 GO BP terms, 1000 perms): ~2–4 minutes, so the only missing input really is the library.

## 4. THE FLAG YOU ASKED FOR — stability

- **Term-level stability cannot be assessed**: with no gene-set library there are zero candidate terms, so "is the lowest-FDR term stable across metrics/designs/size filters" is *unanswerable*, not "stable". I will not present one term as if it were computed.
- **What is assessable — stability of the ranked input itself**: across metrics Spearman 0.90/0.87/0.96 (universe B), but leading-edge overlap is poor (top-500 Jaccard 0.03–0.36) and universe choice changes 444/500 of the top-500. Across designs: leave-out-3_1 r=0.96 (safe), two-factor r=0.72 (moderate: a meaningful share of the leading edge is re-ordered once serum starvation is modelled additively), starved contrast r=0.30 (different question). **Conclusion: the eventual leading term is plausibly sensitive to universe choice and to the metric, less so to replicate-level leverage.** The one-shot script runs all 4 ranked files × max_size 500/1000 so you can read term-level stability off one execution once the library exists.

## 5. CLOSEST DEFENSIBLE STATEMENT (clearly labelled, NOT an enrichment result)

Leading-edge genes from the completed DE (universe B, padj<0.05, strongest log2FC). Up: THBS1, AHRR, CYP1A1, CCN2, LYNX1, ALDH1A3, GDF15, CCN1, KRT7, TP53I3, GDA, COL17A1, CDKN1A (+ FDXR, AEN, BTG2, TP53INP1, TXNRD1, SMAD3 top-by-p). Down: ANKRD37, FOSB, FOS, DDIT3, ARRDC4, PFKFB4, ALDOC, GPI, PDK1, EGLN3, P4HA1, BNIP3, ENO2. Reading these with my prior knowledge (explicitly interpretation, not computation): the up arm is a xenobiotic/AhR response (CYP1A1, AHRR, ALDH1A3) plus p53/DNA-damage and growth-arrest (CDKN1A, GDF15, FDXR, AEN, BTG2, TP53INP1) plus ECM/integrin–YAP targets (THBS1, CCN1, CCN2, COL17A1); the down arm is a hypoxia/glycolysis + ISR signature (ANKRD37, EGLN3, P4HA1, BNIP3, ALDOC, PFKFB4, PDK1, ENO2, DDIT3). If GO BP 2021 were run, my prior would be that the winning terms come from "response to xenobiotic stimulus / cellular response to chemical stimulus" (up) or "cellular response to hypoxia / glycolysis" (down) — a hypothesis to check, not an answer.

## 6. TO UNBLOCK (exactly one artifact)

Either (a) network egress to maayanlab.cloud + `pip install gseapy`, or (b) the single file `data/GO_Biological_Process_2021.gmt` (Enrichr export: `https://maayanlab.cloud/Enrichr/geneSetLibrary?mode=text&libraryName=GO_Biological_Process_2021`). Then `python analysis/gseapy_one_shot.py` runs all four ranked lists at max_size 500 and 1000, 1000 permutations, seed 42, and prints for each the term with the lowest `FDR q-val` plus the lowest-FDR up- and down-regulated terms with term size, NES, nominal p, FDR and leading edge. With only (b) and no gseapy, the same script falls back to the validated engine and labels the output as a gseapy-equivalent run.
